scripts.radio:
Hamjambo wasikilizaji, and welcome to Kenyans Are Asking.

This week, data from the IMF confirmed Kenya has reclaimed its spot as East Africa's largest economy in dollar terms. That is a notable headline, but economic prestige in Washington means very little if it doesn’t translate to dignity and fair distribution in our villages and towns.

Which brings us to an uncomfortable habit we continue to witness: public leaders threatening whole regions with marginalisation over how they voted. Let us be plain. Development projects are not political rewards or personal favours dished out for loyalty. Under our Constitution, access to public infrastructure, clean water, and healthcare is an inherent right funded by your taxes, not the goodwill of an individual in office.

That same rule of integrity must apply to the National Government Constituency Development Fund. Whether your MP wears the colours of the ruling coalition or the opposition, every single bursary shilling must be accounted for on public noticeboards. A school bursary is not an MP's personal charity; it belongs to the children of Kenya.

Finally, as police once again blocked politicians from turning a funeral into a podium this week, we must insist on basic decency. Grief belongs to the bereaved, and public leadership demands respect.

Kwa ufupi: Miradi ya maendeleo na basari za CDF si zawadi au hisani kutoka kwa wanasiasa. Ni haki yako ya kikatiba inayofadhiliwa na kodi zako. Kataa vitisho, na dai uwajibikaji kila wakati.
scripts.voice_note: Habari zenu, here is your weekly brief from Kenyans Are Asking. The IMF says our economy is back at the top in East Africa, but let’s talk about reality on the ground. We are still hearing politicians tell communities that without political loyalty, they won't see development. Let’s reject that completely. Article 43 and Chapter Six of our Constitution are crystal clear: public services and infrastructure are not rewards for good political behaviour. You pay taxes on every loaf of bread, every mobile transfer, and every payslip. That money builds the roads, and that money funds CDF bursaries. No MP is doing your child a personal favour by granting a bursary. Demand full transparency on bursary lists in your ward, respect families at funerals by keeping politics out of burials, and remember: development is your right.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Development and CDF bursaries are your constitutional rights funded by your taxes, not political rewards or personal favors from politicians.
scripts.reels: Ever hear a politician claim that your area won’t see development unless you vote the right way? Remind them of the Constitution. Tarmac, hospitals, and CDF bursaries are funded by your taxes, not political patronage. Under Chapter Six, public officers owe equity to every single Kenyan. Development is your right, not a reward. Demand accountability.
